chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr from one of his companions said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I dislike praying in their mosques.' He said, 'Do not dislike it, for there is no mosque built except upon the grave of a prophet or the successor of a prophet who was killed, and a splash of his blood hit that place, so God loved to be remembered in it. So perform the obligatory prayers and the voluntary prayers in them, and make up what you missed.'

key_terms.مَسَاجِدِهِمْ: their mosques (referring to the mosques of the prophets and Imams)

ai.seo_question: Why should one not dislike praying in the mosques of the righteous or prophets according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a metaphysical justification for the sanctity of mosques by linking them to the graves of prophets or their successors (A'imma), where a splash of their blood landed, making them beloved places for God's remembrance. This narration, found in Shaykh al-Tusi's *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, encourages believers to pray both obligatory and voluntary prayers in these spaces, including making up missed prayers, thereby affirming the spiritual continuity between the divine message and the Imams. This view underscores the Shia belief in the intrinsic holiness of the Ahl al-Bayt, extending their reverence to the physical spaces associated with them.
